ORDR_CATEGORY.description: Server-side Ordr device-category predicate forwarded as the category=<value> query parameter on GET /api/v1/devices and GET /api/v1/alerts. Optional; empty / blank walks the entire tenant's inventory across every device class (the operator's token scope still applies). Forwarded verbatim — Ordr accepts both the literal category label (e.g. 'medical', 'iot', 'ot', 'it') and the numeric category id depending on tenant configuration. Useful for sharding inventory pulls across multiple discovery profiles so each dispatcher agent only walks one device-class worth of inventory per run. Whitespace is trimmed.

ORDR_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional Faraday severity floor (case-insensitive 'info' / 'low' / 'medium' / 'high' / 'critical'); records whose mapped severity is strictly below the floor are dropped client-side after the fetch. Device records (no severity of their own) are bucketed from the Ordr criticality field (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info, or 0..4 numeric); alerts use the published severity field directly (label or 0..10 numeric, falling back to risk_score when severity is missing). Closed / Resolved / Muted / Suppressed / Dismissed alerts are floored to 'info' regardless of the published bucket (preserved via an explicit Ordr-Status pivot). Operator-friendly aliases are accepted ('informational' -> 'info', 'moderate' -> 'medium', 'crit' -> 'critical', 'elevated' -> 'high', 'severe' -> 'critical', 'none' -> 'info'). Blank / missing / unparseable values keep every record (the typical operational mode for first-time imports).

name: ordr
title: Ordr
description: Ordr OT / IoT / IoMT device and alert importer. Pulls connected-device inventory and security alerts from an Ordr Core tenant via its v1 REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Ordr is a connected-device security platform that fingerprints OT / IoT / IoMT / IT endpoints (medical devices, building-automation controllers, manufacturing PLCs, clinical IT endpoints, IT-side jump hosts that touch the connected-device segment) from passive collector traffic and surfaces both the resulting device inventory and rule-based / anomaly alerts via a REST surface. Endpoints used: (1) GET /api/v1/devices?category=<cat>&page=N&page_size=M (paginated connected-device inventory; canonical envelope {'results': [...], 'count': N, 'next': '...', 'previous': '...'} with each record carrying id, name, ip, mac, manufacturer / vendor, model, firmware / firmware_version, os / operating_system, category / device_type, criticality, location / site_name, first_seen / last_seen, risk_score 0..100, and an optional cve_list / vulnerabilities list); (2) GET /api/v1/alerts?category=<cat>&page=N&page_size=M (paginated security alert feed; same envelope shape with each record carrying id, title / name, description, severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info, or 0..10 numeric), category (Anomaly / Policy Violation / Known Threat / Vulnerability — Ordr's published alert taxonomy), status (Open / Resolved / Muted / Suppressed), created_at / updated_at (or created / updated on older firmwares), device_id / related_devices list of device ids or scalar ip strings the alert is keyed on, device_type, and risk_score). Auth: Ordr's v1 surface uses a long-lived API-token flow — the token is provisioned in the Ordr console and passed verbatim as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every /api/v1/ request (no login exchange). ORDR_HOST is the tenant base URL (Ordr is deployed both as on-prem and as SaaS so there is no global default — the executor exits cleanly when missing); whitespace is trimmed and https:// is added when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Pagination is one-based via page=N + page_size=M; walks until len(records) < page_size or the env-only ORDR_PAGES knob is reached (default 10, clamped to [1, 100]). 401 short-circuits the whole executor (token is wrong); 403 / 429 / 5xx stop pagination on this surface and return what we have. Each Ordr record becomes one Faraday host. Device records project ip onto host.ip (loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are skipped, falling back to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel), name onto host.hostnames, mac onto host.mac, and the manufacturer / model / firmware / os chain joins onto host.os; the device itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so connected-device inventory entries land alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Armis, Axonius, Device42, Fleet, runZero, Jamf Pro). Alert records are keyed on the first related_devices IP (falling back to the alert's own src_ip / dst_ip / ip field, then 0.0.0.0 for policy-shaped alerts not keyed on any single device); the alert title lands on host.hostnames and the description / severity / category enrichment is embedded in the vulnerability description. Severity bucketing: devices use the criticality field (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info label or 0..4 numeric, falling back to 0..10 for tenants that surface criticality as a raw score); alerts use severity directly (label or 0..10 numeric, falling back to risk_score). Closed / Resolved / Muted / Suppressed / Dismissed alerts are floored to 'info' regardless of the published severity (preserved via an explicit Ordr-Status pivot). Unparseable / missing severity defaults to 'info'. Status is always 'open' so the operator's remediation workflow takes over; the closed state is preserved via the info-severity floor + the Ordr-Status pivot. Refs include explicit Ordr-DeviceID / Ordr-AlertID / Ordr-Location / Ordr-Category / Ordr-Type / Ordr-Criticality / Ordr-Manufacturer / Ordr-Model / Ordr-Firmware / Ordr-OS / Ordr-Severity / Ordr-Status / Ordr-RiskScore / Ordr-FirstSeen / Ordr-LastSeen / Ordr-CreatedAt / Ordr-UpdatedAt pivots, plus the canonical NVD CVE permalink for any CVE ids surfaced in the cve_list / vulnerabilities / description / title fields. Tags: [ordr, ot-security, device|alert].
